review.material: The publisher-deposited abstract in Crossref was read in full. The publisher page was rate-limited.
review.limitations: The complete chapter, its exercises and any detailed assessment evidence were not inspected.

evidence.description: Primary abstract deposited with the DOI record.
Original publication link; full chapter not reviewed.

sections.title: What it is about
sections.text: Knight presents teaching shape grammars through reflective visual and manual computation. Slow refers to an approach to understanding and exploration, not to inefficient code.

sections.title: Premise
sections.text: The chapter argues that expressive, perceptual and interpretive aspects of shape grammars deserve attention alongside fast automated generation.

sections.title: Teaching approach reported
sections.text: The abstract describes manual work within a collaborative learning-by-making environment and an overview of teaching at MIT. It considers opportunities and difficulties in combining slow human computation with machine computation.

sections.title: Stated contribution
sections.text: The contribution is a pedagogical account and discussion. The abstract supplies no participant numbers, assessment scores or controlled comparison of educational outcomes.

sections.title: Reading boundary
sections.text: Specific exercises and any qualifications in the chapter remain unreviewed. The abstract is insufficient evidence that manual computation is always educationally superior.

sections.title: A practical reading prompt
sections.text: Try carrying out one rule application by hand and explain the perception and transformation decisions you made. Then ask what automation would reveal, hide or make easier.

terms.meaning: Reflective, manually performed visual computation, as framed in this pedagogical chapter.
